name: Convex public function surface being enumerated (prod)
description: PAGE — owner: marcelo. More than 25 DISTINCT Convex function paths failed with EMPTY arguments in 15 minutes. That is somebody walking the API surface, not an application bug.

WHY EMPTY ARGS IS THE PREDICATE, not the error text. An enumerator calls every name it has with `{}` to learn which exist and what they take, so its calls carry ~4 argument bytes and touch each path exactly once. Real breakage is the opposite shape: a handful of paths, many times, with real arguments. Counting distinct paths alone is NOT enough — on 2026-09-10T09:00Z a Convex concurrency saturation event ('limited to 256 concurrent querys') failed 47 distinct paths in one bin and would have paged this rule. Only 31% of that bin's calls had empty args, against 91-98% for the scan, so the empty-args filter separates the two cleanly and leaves capacity incidents to the monitors that own them.

MEASURED BASELINE (7 days to 2026-09-16, 15-minute windows): 65 windows have any empty-argument failure at all. The highest legitimate value is 18 (the concurrency event above), next 13, p95 = 13. The 2026-09-16 reconnaissance scan produced 397 and 357. The threshold of 25 sits ~39% above the worst honest observation and roughly 15x below the incident, which is why it is set here rather than at the p99 of an unfiltered path count.

WHAT IT CATCHES, AND HOW EARLY. The 2026-09-16 scan ran in three phases: empty-argument enumeration of ~400 paths (07:37-07:40Z), an authorization probe with synthetic ids (07:41-07:50Z), then a sweep of mutations and actions (07:50-07:55Z). This rule fires in phase 1, about 13 minutes before the write sweep — the phase that can actually change state if any handler is missing a guard. Nothing detected that incident; it was noticed by a human reading #mcpjam-alerts.

WHAT IT CANNOT DO. Convex's own logs carry no caller identity, so this rule reports shape only. Attribution comes from Sentry, whose Convex integration stamps `user` and `user.ip` on every event — see the `convex-api-scan-response` skill, section 3. A slow scanner that pauses between calls, or one that sends plausible arguments, stays under this threshold; this is a cheap tripwire for the common loud case, not a rate limiter.
TRIAGE — confirm the shape, then name the caller:

['mcpjam-backend-prod'] | where tostring(['data.topic']) == 'function_execution' and tostring(['data.status']) == 'failure' | extend ab = todouble(['data.usage.function_args_bytes']) | summarize N = count(), Paths = dcount(tostring(['data.function.path'])), Empty = countif(ab <= 8) by bin(_time, 5m) | sort by _time desc

Paths approximately equal to N, and Empty approximately equal to N, confirms enumeration. Then run the Sentry aggregation in the skill to get the guest id or account and the source IP. Containment is the caller's session: Cloudflare cannot see this traffic, because the Convex deployment answers on *.convex.cloud / *.convex.site and is never proxied through our zone. Do not report an edge rule as containment.

AFTERWARDS: run the authorization audit in that skill (scripts/audit_surface.py) over the paths the scanner reached. Convex echoes the full argument validator in ArgumentValidationError, so an enumerator always leaves with the schema — authorization, not obscurity, is the control, and the audit is what confirms it held.
ROLLBACK: revert the definition file, then run `node ops/axiom-monitors/apply.mjs --apply --only convex-surface-enumeration`. The --apply flag is required; the script defaults to read-only plan mode.
